Prehistory: Period of human history before records.
Considered the ideal man in Hindu tradition, this seventh avatar of the god Vishnu was born in Ayodhya to King Dasaratha and later married Sita — who is he?
Mixing anti-elitist rhetoric with neo-nationalism, social conservatism, and a vow to defend national culture from outsiders — which political ideology is this?

Right-wing populism: Political ideology. Right-wing populism, also called right populism and national populism, is a political ideology that combines right-wing politics with populist rhetoric and themes.
Often called the first European war of the 21st century, this August 2008 conflict erupted over the breakaway regions of South Ossetia and Abkhazia — which war?
Russo-Georgian War: 2008 war between Russia and Georgia.
After leaving office, she traded the Finnish prime minister's chair for a desk at the Tony Blair Institute, advising on leadership reform — which young Social Democrat was she?
Sanna Marin: Prime Minister of Finland from 2019 to 2023.
A veteran of the Soviet-Afghan and Chechen wars, this Russian air-force chief was reportedly sacked by Putin over ties to the Wagner Group rebellion — who is he?
Existing from 57 BCE to 935 CE and forming the Three Kingdoms of Korea alongside Paekche and Goguryeo, which kingdom had the smallest population of the three?
Silla: Korean kingdom (57 BCE–935 CE). Silla was one of the longest-lasting countries in Korean history.
This leading man of 1950s Westerns and film noir later played General Jack D. Ripper in Dr. Strangelove and Captain McCluskey in The Godfather — who is he?
A teacher, Marxist, and philosopher honored as a "Father of the Republic of Indonesia," this independence fighter founded the Murba Party and lived the life of a guerrilla and spy — who was he?
Tan Malaka: Indonesian communist philosopher, activist, and national hero (1897–1949)
Brother of King Henry VIII's third wife, this nobleman married the king's widow Catherine Parr in 1547 while sparring with his own brother for influence over the young King Edward VI — who was he?
Thomas Seymour, 1st Baron Seymour of Sudeley
Thomas Seymour, 1st Baron Seymour of Sudeley: English nobleman (1508–1548)
Thomas Seymour, 1st Baron Seymour of Sudeley
Dubbed 'the Nelson of the East' by Western reporters, this Imperial Japanese Navy admiral penned Russia's fleet into Port Arthur before a decisive 1905 victory at Tsushima — who is he?

Spanning roughly 800 to 1050 CE, this era of Norse raiding, trading, and settlement saw Scandinavians reach as far as Newfoundland, becoming the first Europeans known to set foot in North America. What period was this?
Viking Age: Period of European history (about 800–1050)
Fought from December 1812 to May 1814, this multinational alliance of European powers finally defeated Napoleon's empire and forced him into exile on Elba — which conflict?
War of the Sixth Coalition: 1813–1814 conflict during the Napoleonic Wars.
Commander of the Indonesian Armed Forces during the country's 1998 transition from authoritarian rule, this retired general later chaired the Presidential Advisory Council — who is it?
Wiranto: Indonesian general and politician. On 27 July 2016, Wiranto was appointed Coordinating Minister for Political, Legal, and Security Affairs, replacing Luhut Binsar Panjaitan.
A graduate of Cairo University who briefly served as Japan's defense minister in 2007, this politician has governed Tokyo since 2016 — who is she?
Yuriko Koike: Governor of Tokyo since 2016. Yuriko Koike (Japanese: 小池 百合子, Hepburn: Koike Yuriko; born 15 July 1952) is a Japanese politician who has served as the Governor of Tokyo since 2016.
Which one below was born first?
Joseph Schumpeter (born 1883) is the earliest of the four. Joseph Alois Schumpeter (German: [ˈʃʊmpeːtɐ]; February 8, 1883 – January 8, 1950) was an Austrian political economist.
Which of these four was born earliest?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four. Henry Vaughan (1621 – 23 April 1695) was a Welsh metaphysical poet, author and translator writing in English, and a medical physician.
Which of these people was born first?
Jīvaka (born 401 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four began earliest?
C++ (founded 1983) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is an astronomer?
Annie Jump Cannon is an astronomer.
Which of these is a mathematician?
Ted Kaczynski is a mathematician. The FBI used the case identifier UNABOM (University and Airline Bombing) before his identity was known, resulting in the media naming him the "Unabomber".
What is the atomic number of Palladium?
Palladium: Palladium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Pd and atomic number 46.
What is the atomic number of Potassium?
Potassium: Potassium is a chemical element; it has symbol K (from Neo-Latin kalium) and atomic number 19.
In what year was Sergei Korolev born?
Sergei Korolev: Originally trained as an aircraft designer, Korolev became a leading figure in Soviet rocketry.
In what year was Nostradamus born?
Nostradamus: Nostradamus's father's family had originally been Jewish, but had converted to Catholic Christianity a generation before Nostradamus was born.
In what year was Tim Berners-Lee born?
Tim Berners-Lee: Berners-Lee was previously a senior researcher and holder of the 3Com founder's chair at the MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL).
In what year did Steve Jobs die?
Steve Jobs: Steven Paul Jobs (February 24, 1955 – October 5, 2011) was an American businessman, inventor, and investor.
In what year did Alan Turing die?
Alan Turing: Alan Mathison Turing (23 June 1912 – 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, philosopher and theoretical biologist.
In what year was Andromeda Galaxy discovered?
Andromeda Galaxy: The Andromeda Galaxy is a barred spiral galaxy and is the nearest major galaxy to the Milky Way.
Pillars of Creation: National Aeronautics and Space Administration. The astronomers responsible for the photo were Jeff Hester and Paul Scowen from Arizona State University.
Which company manufactures KAI T-50 Golden Eagle?
KAI T-50 Golden Eagle: Korea Aerospace Industries. It is South Korea's first indigenous supersonic aircraft and one of the world's few supersonic trainers.
In which country is Convair B-58 Hustler based?
Convair B-58 Hustler: United States. The Convair B-58 Hustler is a supersonic strategic bomber, the first capable of Mach 2 flight.
Who is credited with discovering Rutherfordium?
Rutherfordium: Albert Ghiorso. Rutherfordium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rf and atomic number 104.
Who is credited with discovering Ampère's force law?
Ampère's force law: André-Marie Ampère. In magnetostatics, Ampère's force law describes the force of attraction or repulsion between two current-carrying wires.
Who is credited with discovering Rhenium?
Rhenium: Walter Noddack. Rhenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Re and atomic number 75.

Despite resembling an unrelated shrub in leaf and flower shape, this shade-loving carrot-family plant has spread worldwide as an invasive garden escapee since being introduced as an ornamental — what is it?
Aegopodium podagraria is a species of flowering plant in the carrot family Apiaceae that grows in shady places.
Endemic to the rainforests of Sumatra, this plant grows an enormous inflorescence that blooms only rarely and briefly, emitting the stench of rotting flesh to lure pollinators — what plant is it?
Amorphophallus titanum is a flowering plant in the family Araceae.
Most often caused by stroke or head trauma, which condition impairs a person's ability to comprehend or formulate language because specific brain regions aren't working?
Aphasia is an impairment in a person's ability to comprehend or formulate language because of dysfunction in specific brain regions.
These large Old World monkeys come in six distinct species, each native to a different region of Africa, with one species also found on the Arabian Peninsula — what primate is it?
Baboon are primates comprising the genus Papio, one of the 23 genera of Old World monkeys, in the family Cercopithecidae.
From molecules and cells up to whole ecosystems, this science studies living things through ideas like heredity, evolution, and homeostasis — what is it?
Biology is the scientific study of life and living organisms.
Present in both sexes from the same embryonic tissue, these two prominences on the upper torso permanently enlarge only in human females at puberty, driven by estrogen and growth hormone - name them?
Breast are two prominences located on the upper ventral region of the torso in humans and other primates.
Discovered in 1940, this non-intoxicating compound extracted from cannabis is used medically as an anticonvulsant for two rare, severe forms of childhood epilepsy — what is it?
Cannabidiol (CBD) is a phytocannabinoid, one of 113 identified cannabinoids in Cannabis, along with tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), and accounts for up to 40% of the plant's extract.
First cultivated in Mesoamerica and later spread worldwide during the Columbian Exchange, this edible gourd-family plant is also known as christophine, mirliton, or choko — what is it?

Chayote (previously placed in the obsolete genus Sechium, now in the genus Sicyos, as Sicyos edulis), also known as christophine, mirliton, gisquil, and choko, is an edible plant belonging to the gourd family, Cucurbitaceae.
Its glorious blue in glass and paint was long wrongly blamed on bismuth, and frustrated miners named its ore after a goblin. Which hard, gray element carries the symbol Co?
Cobalt is a chemical element; it has symbol Co and atomic number 27.
Which vanilla-scented, benzopyrone lactone compound acts as a plant's chemical defense against predators and, via its derivatives, gave rise to the anticoagulant warfarin?
Coumarin is an aromatic organic chemical compound with formula C9H6O2.
The word names both a noun — a plan or proposal made by a thinking agent — and a verb for developing one, always aiming to satisfy goals while weighing function and aesthetics; what is it?
Design is the concept or proposal for an object, process, or system.
Partly blinded in a childhood fishing accident, this Alabama-born naturalist turned to insects, co-developed the theory of island biogeography, and founded the field of sociobiology. Who is he?
E. O. Wilson (June 10, 1929 - December 26, 2021) was an American biologist, naturalist, ecologist, and entomologist who developed the field of sociobiology.
Also known as human herpesvirus 4, this common virus was the first identified oncogenic virus and causes infectious mononucleosis in 90% of cases. What is it?
Epstein–Barr virus (EBV), also known as human herpesvirus 4 (HHV-4), is one of the nine known human herpesvirus types in the herpes family, and is one of the most common viruses in humans.
Which group of vascular plants, which reproduce via spores rather than seeds or flowers, are known for their large megaphyll leaves and the coiled 'fiddleheads' many species unfurl as new growth?
Fern (Polypodiopsida or Polypodiophyta) are a group of vascular plants (land plants with vascular tissues such as xylem and phloem) that reproduce via spores and have neither seeds nor flowers.

Lasting anywhere from milliseconds to hours, these are the most luminous explosions in the universe after the Big Bang, sometimes triggered when massive stars collapse into black holes — what are they?
Gamma-ray burst (GRBs) are extremely energetic events occurring in distant galaxies that represent the brightest and most powerful class of explosion in the Universe.
Comprising about 50 species native to tropical regions worldwide, this genus produces roughly 80% of the world's natural fiber and doubles as an oilseed crop — which genus?
Gossypium is a genus of flowering plants in the tribe Gossypieae of the mallow family, Malvaceae, from which cotton is harvested.

Linked to conditions like tuberculosis, bronchitis, and lung cancer, this medical term describes blood discharged from the airway rather than internal bleeding elsewhere in the body. What is it called?
Hemoptysis is the discharge of blood or blood-stained mucus through the mouth coming from the bronchi, larynx, trachea, or lungs.
Sold as a 3 percent solution for the bathroom cabinet but explosive when concentrated, this oxidizer and antiseptic carries the formula H2O2 — what is it?
Hydrogen peroxide is a chemical compound with the formula H2O2.
In Kevin Costner's directorial debut, a Union army lieutenant travels to the American frontier and comes to live among a group of Lakota. What 1990 film is it?
Iridium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ir and atomic number 77.
Court astronomer and advisor to Elizabeth I, this mathematician and alchemist kept one of England's largest libraries and is credited with coining the phrase 'British Empire' — who was he?
John Dee (13 July 1527 - December 1608 or March 1609) was an English mathematician, astronomer, teacher, astrologer, occultist, and alchemist.
Despite its name suggesting a root vegetable, this biennial cultivar of wild cabbage grows a swollen edible stem above ground and is related to broccoli, kale, and Brussels sprouts — what is it?
Kohlrabi (scientific name Brassica oleracea Gongylodes Group), also called German turnip or turnip cabbage, is a biennial vegetable, a low, stout cultivar of wild cabbage.
Found in the support tissues of most plants, this polymer resists rot and reinforces wood and bark structure — what is it?
Lignin is a class of complex organic polymers that form key structural materials in the support tissues of most plants.
This genus of Old World monkeys includes 23 species ranging from Asia and North Africa all the way to Gibraltar, and mostly eats fruit — what is it?
Macaque (Macaca) of gregarious Old World monkeys of the subfamily Cercopithecinae.

Designed as both fighter and ground-attack aircraft (hence the F/A designation), this all-weather supersonic, carrier-capable twin-engined jet was derived from the YF-17 and developed for the Navy. What aircraft is this?

McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet is an all-weather supersonic, twin-engined, carrier-capable, multirole combat aircraft, designed as both a fighter and ground attack aircraft (hence the F/A designation).
Also called selective sound sensitivity syndrome, this disorder causes specific everyday sounds to trigger intense, disproportionate emotional and physiological distress — what is it?
Misophonia (or selective sound sensitivity syndrome) is a disorder of decreased tolerance to specific sounds or their associated stimuli, or cues.
Found from Africa to Southeast Asia, this snake genus contains the 'true cobras' as opposed to look-alikes like the king cobra — which genus?
Naja is a genus of venomous elapid snakes commonly known as cobras (or "true cobras").
Built from nucleotide units of a sugar, a phosphate, and a nitrogenous base, these biomolecules come in two main classes distinguished by whether their sugar is ribose or deoxyribose — what are they?
Nucleic acid are large biomolecules that are crucial in all cells and viruses.
Belonging to the pea family and native to Mesoamerica, this vine produces blue or white flowers and an edible tuberous root known in Spanish as jícama — which species?
Pachyrhizus erosus (from Nahuatl languages: xicamatl) or Mexican turnip, is a native Mesoamerican vine, although the name jicama most commonly refers to the plant's edible tuberous root.
This serous membrane lines the abdominal cavity, wrapping most internal organs in a single sheet of mesothelium that also carries their blood vessels and nerves — what's the membrane?
Peritoneum is the serous membrane forming the lining of the abdominal cavity or coelom in amniotes and some invertebrates, such as annelids.

This common skin condition begins with a single scaly 'herald patch,' followed weeks later by an eruption of smaller pinkish spots, and typically clears on its own within three months. What is it called?
Pityriasis rosea is a type of skin rash.

An Italian chemist and Auschwitz survivor, he wrote a celebrated memoir of his year in the camp and later a book of stories each named for a chemical element, hailed as the best science book ever — who was he?
Primo Levi (31 July 1919 - 11 April 1987) was a Jewish Italian chemist, partisan, Holocaust survivor and writer.
This Indian Air Force pilot became the first Indian ever to travel to space, flying aboard a Soviet Soyuz mission in 1984 — who is he?
Rakesh Sharma (born 13 January 1949) is an Indian cosmonaut and a pilot of the Indian Air Force.
Named for its type genus, this plant family of nearly 4,800 species includes the trees and shrubs behind apples, pears, plums, cherries, and peaches — what family is it?
Rosaceae is a family of flowering plants that includes 4,828 known species in 91 genera.

Native to the North Pacific coasts, this marine mammal is the heaviest member of the weasel family yet one of the smallest marine mammals, insulated by the densest fur coat in the animal kingdom — what is it?
Sea otter (Enhydra lutris) is a marine mammal native to the coasts of the northern and eastern North Pacific Ocean.
Despite the name, this digestive organ is about 6.5 metres long; it's just narrower in diameter than its large counterpart. What organ is it?
Small intestine is an organ in the gastrointestinal tract where most of the absorption of nutrients from food takes place.
CEO of Microsoft from 2000 to 2014, this American businessman later became the billionaire owner of the Los Angeles Clippers — who is he?
Steve Ballmer (born March 24, 1956) is an American businessman and investor who was the chief executive officer of Microsoft from 2000 to 2014.
Found naturally in grapes and other fruits, this crystalline compound's potassium salt is better known as cream of tartar, a key ingredient in homemade baking powder — which compound?
Tartaric acid is a white, crystalline organic acid that occurs naturally in many fruits, most notably in grapes but also in tamarinds, bananas, avocados, and citrus.
This family of large, long-legged flies can be identified by a maxillary-palp segment longer than the other three combined, and typically has thirteen segments in each antenna. Name the family?
Tipulidae is a family of large crane flies in the order Diptera.
This bodily fluid, produced by the kidneys to flush out urea and other waste, can also serve a second life as a nitrogen-rich fertilizer for soil — what is it?
Urine is the fluid excreted by the kidneys of vertebrates to clear the bloodstream of excess water and metabolic by-products including urea, uric acid, and creatinine.
Intermediate in size between the Greyhound and the Italian Greyhound, this gentle, minimal-shedding sighthound turns into a bundle of energy the moment it's outdoors — which breed?
Whippet is a British breed of sighthound. It closely resembles the Greyhound and the smaller Italian Greyhound, and is intermediate between them in size.
Named for its standard passenger capacity, this twin-engine turboprop regional airliner is assembled in Toulouse by a Franco-Italian manufacturer that is half-owned by Airbus — what aircraft is this?
ATR 72: Regional turboprop airliner. The ATR 72 is a twin-engine turboprop, short-haul regional airliner developed and produced in France and Italy by aircraft manufacturer ATR.
Sold as button, cremini, or portobello depending on its stage of maturity, this cultivated mushroom is grown in more than 70 countries — what species is it?
Agaricus bisporus: Species of fungus. Agaricus bisporus, commonly known as the cultivated mushroom, is a basidiomycete mushroom native to grasslands in Eurasia and North America.
Approved for medical use in the US in 1966, this xanthine oxidase inhibitor lowers uric acid to prevent gout and certain kidney stones — what medication is it?
Allopurinol: Medication. Allopurinol is a medication used to decrease high blood uric acid levels.
Comprising more than 140 species across 16 genera, this small, oily forage fish is found everywhere from the Atlantic to the Black Sea — what is it?
Known by common names like greenfly and blackfly, these small sap-sucking insects reproduce via live-born nymphs without males, a trick called telescoping generations — what are they?
Aphid: Superfamily of insects. The group includes the fluffy white woolly aphids.
First described in 1740 under the name Compositae, this enormous flowering-plant family includes daisies, asters and sunflowers — what is it?
Asteraceae: Large family of flowering plants.
A sessile marine arthropod related to crabs and lobsters, folklore once claimed geese hatched fully formed from one variety of it — what creature is it?
Barnacle: Subclass of sessile marine crustaceans.
This English musician played bass on the Rolling Stones' first nineteen studio albums across three decades before later fronting his own blues outfit, the Rhythm Kings — who is he?

A twin-engine, carrier-capable strike fighter flown by the U.S., Australia, and Kuwait, this larger, more advanced follow-on to an earlier 1980s Navy jet packs an internal 20 mm rotary cannon and can be rigged as an airborne refueling tanker — what is it called?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Boeing F/A-18E/F Super Hornet: Series of carrier-based multirole combat aircraft.
Despite the name, this pseudocereal isn't related to true cereals at all — it's kin to rhubarb and sorrel, and was first cultivated in Yunnan around 6,000 BC — which crop is it?
Buckwheat: Species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae.
This suborder of 'dog-like' carnivores includes bears, raccoons, weasels, and seals, and is thought to have diversified mainly across North America and northern Eurasia — what's it called?
Caniformia: Suborder of mammals. Caniformia is a suborder within the order Carnivora consisting of "dog-like" carnivorans.
Named for barbels that resemble a cat's whiskers, these scaleless, ray-finned fish include giants like the Mekong species and go by nicknames such as 'mud cat' in the Southern US — what are they?
Catfish: Order of fish. Catfish are a diverse group of ray-finned fish of the order Siluriformes (historically Nematognathi).

One of the earliest cultivated legumes — its oldest traces were unearthed in Syria — this protein-packed seed goes by names like garbanzo and chana, and forms the backbone of hummus and falafel. What is it?
Chickpea: Species of flowering plant with edible seeds.
This English inventor made the world's first slimline pocket calculator in 1972, then launched the UK's first mass-market home computer for under £100 — who is he?
Clive Sinclair: English entrepreneur and inventor (1940–2021)
A heavy-set, fox-like canid native to East Asia, this animal is named for its raccoon-like face markings and is unusual among canids for hibernating in winter and climbing trees. What is this animal?
Common raccoon dog: Canid indigenous to East Asia. Named for its raccoon-like face markings, it is most closely related to foxes.

An incurable, always fatal neurodegenerative disease belonging to the transmissible spongiform encephalopathy group, it causes early symptoms like memory problems, behavioral changes, and poor coordination, with about 70% of sufferers dying within a year. What disease is it?
Known as Queen Anne's lace, this Old World wildflower is the wild ancestor of the cultivated carrot — what is it?
Daucus carota: Species of flowering plant.
A Cambridge-educated lecturer in English literature, this Hashemite princess briefly reigned as Queen of Jordan as King Hussein's first wife — who is she?
Dina bint Abdul-Hamid: Queen of Jordan from 1955 to 1957.
Known as 'crawling' pinnipeds to distinguish them from their eared, sea-lion-like cousins, this group's only completely freshwater population lives in Lake Baikal — what are they called?
This branch of biology and medicine studies the glands that secrete hormones directly into the bloodstream, governing everything from growth to mood and metabolism — what is it called?
Endocrinology: Branch of medicine pertaining to the endocrine system.
Commonly called spurge, this giant plant genus includes the popular Christmas poinsettia and a thorny succulent nicknamed 'crown of thorns' — which genus is it?
This subfamily of cats, distinguished by a bony hyoid that lets its members purr instead of roar, is informally known as the small cats — which subfamily?
Felinae: Subfamily of Felidae. The Felinae or small cats are a subfamily of the Felidae distinguished by a bony hyoid, because of which they can purr but not roar.
This infection and inflammation of hair follicles produces pimples with white tips anywhere on hair-covered skin — what is the condition called?
Folliculitis: Human and animal disease of follicles.

Named after Scottish naturalist Alexander Garden and first proposed in 1753 by botanist Jane Colden, this fragrant flowering genus in the coffee family is native to Africa, Asia and Australia — which plant genus?
Gardenia: Genus of flowering plants in the coffee family Rubiaceae.

This general term covers any organ that secretes substances either straight into the bloodstream, like endocrine ones, or through a duct to a body surface, like exocrine ones — what type of structure is it?
Gland: Type of animal organ. A gland may also function to remove unwanted substances such as urine from the body.
Known to the British as the Martlet, this American carrier-based fighter entered service in 1940 and remained the U.S. Navy's best fighter against the Mitsubishi Zero until mid-1943 — which aircraft?
Grumman F4F Wildcat: United States Navy World War II era fighter plane.
A 1930s-40s Hollywood star of films like Algiers, she also co-invented a radio guidance system during WWII — which glamorous on-screen inventor was she?
Hedy Lamarr: Austrian-American actress and inventor (1914–2000)
Known as the great apes, this primate family holds eight living species across four genera — orangutans, gorillas, chimps and bonobos, plus one more: us. What is it?
Hominidae: Family of primates. The original meaning of "hominid" referred only to humans (Homo) and their closest extinct relatives.
It usually causes no symptoms at all, yet this persistently elevated arterial pressure is a leading cause of stroke, heart failure and premature death worldwide — what's the medical name for it?
Hypertension: Long-term high blood pressure in the arteries.
This sleep disorder makes it hard to fall or stay asleep, leaving daytime drowsiness, irritability and trouble focusing in its wake — what's its clinical name?
Insomnia: Disorder causing trouble with sleeping.
This U.S. Marine Corps test pilot commanded SpaceX's Crew-7 mission and served as a flight engineer aboard the ISS during Expedition 69/70 — who is she?
Jasmin Moghbeli: NASA astronaut and US Marine Corps officer and test pilot (born 1983)
A 1983 MacArthur Fellow, this American mathematician's work on Hilbert's tenth problem proved crucial to its eventual resolution — now known as the MRDP theorem. Who was she?
This colorless noble gas defined the length of the metre from 1960 to 1983, based on the wavelength of one of its spectral lines — which element?
Krypton: Chemical element with atomic number 36 (Kr)
Also called Hansen's disease, this slow bacterial infection dulls the body's sense of pain so badly that unnoticed injuries can cost a person their fingers and toes — what is it?
Leprosy: Chronic disease caused by bacterial infection.
Born as a Skunk Works black project and nicknamed "Habu," this Mach 3+ reconnaissance aircraft carried a crew of two in tandem cockpits — which plane is it?
Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird: US Air Force supersonic aircraft, 1964–1998.
First named in 1703 to honor a French botanist, this genus of 200-plus flowering trees and shrubs produces large fragrant blooms and cone-like autumn fruits — which genus?
Magnolia: Genus of angiosperms. Magnolia is a large genus of about 210 to 340 flowering plant species in the subfamily Magnolioideae of the family Magnoliaceae.
Awarded the 1918 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering energy quanta, this German physicist originated quantum theory and lent his name to a fundamental physical constant — who is he?
Sold under the brand name Robaxin and developed in 1956, this centrally acting muscle relaxant treats short-term musculoskeletal pain but its exact mechanism remains unclear — what is it?
Methocarbamol: Medication for musculoskeletal pain. It may be used together with rest, physical therapy, and pain medication.
Most under a millimeter long, these eight-legged arachnids include the parasite that plagues honeybee colonies and the species behind scabies in humans — what are they?
Its Inuktitut name means 'the bearded one,' and males emit a strong odor during rut to attract mates — which thick-coated Arctic mammal is this?
Muskox: Species of arctic land mammal.
Erected by entomologist Francis Walker back in 1855, this genus of moths belongs to the family Lasiocampidae — which genus?

This healthcare profession blends the art and science of caring, focusing on protecting and promoting health, preventing illness, and easing suffering through compassionate, hands-on care — what field is it?
Nursing: Health care profession. Nurses may help coordinate care performed by other providers or act independently as nursing professionals.
Named from Greek words meaning 'porous bones,' this disorder causes bone density loss serious enough that fractures can occur with minor stress, especially in the elderly — what is it?
Osteoporosis: Skeletal disorder. Osteoporosis is the most common reason for a broken bone among the elderly.
Also known as trisomy 13, this chromosomal condition arises when cells carry extra genetic material from chromosome 13, causing widespread organ defects — which syndrome?
Patau syndrome: Chromosomal disorder in which there are three copies of chromosome 13.
Synthesized in 1938 by German chemist Otto Eisleb and later marketed as Demerol, this synthetic opioid was the go-to pain medication for much of the 20th century — what is it?
Pethidine: Opioid analgesic. Pethidine, also known as meperidine and sold under the brand name Demerol among others, is a fully synthetic opioid pain medication of the phenylpiperidine class.
Also called threadworm in the UK and seatworm elsewhere, this common intestinal roundworm spreads via the faecal-oral route and is especially prevalent among children — what parasite is it?
A purplish-black crystalline salt that dissolves into an intensely pink-to-purple solution, this strong oxidizer also appears on the WHO's List of Essential Medicines for wound care — what is it?
The earliest vertebrates known to achieve powered flight, these warm-blooded Mesozoic reptiles had wings stretched from ankle to a dramatically lengthened fourth finger — what were they called?
Pterosaur: Extinct order of flying reptiles.
Belonging to the genus Corvus and distinguished from its close relatives mainly by size, the largest species in this bird category are also the largest of all perching birds — which bird?
Raven: Index of animals with the same common name.
This Israeli-American mathematician shared the 2005 Nobel in Economics with Thomas Schelling for illuminating conflict and cooperation through game theory — who is he?
Caused by bacteria in the Salmonella genus, this common form of food poisoning brings diarrhea, fever, and cramps within 12 to 36 hours of eating contaminated food — what is it called?
Salmonellosis: Infection caused by Salmonella bacteria. It is one of the most common diseases to be known as food poisoning (though the name refers to food-borne illness in general).

Caused by a sudden burst of synchronized electrical activity in the brain, this neurological event affects roughly 50 million people worldwide and can range from a brief blank stare to a full convulsion — what is it?
Seizure: Period of symptoms due to excessive or synchronous neuronal brain activity.
This structural framework supporting an animal's body can take the form of a rigid outer shell, an internal bony frame, or simply fluid pressure inside the body. What is it?
Skeleton: Part of the body that forms the supporting structure.

Encased by the vertebral column and running from the brainstem down to about the first lumbar vertebra, this hollow, fluid-filled structure forms the other half of the central nervous system alongside the brain — what is it?
Spinal cord: Part of the vertebral column in animals.
Made by chlorinating ordinary table sugar and roughly 600 times sweeter than it, what is this sugar substitute also known by the E number E955?
Nicknamed water bears and moss piglets, these eight-legged micro-animals shrug off extreme heat, crushing pressure, and even radiation. What are they?
This French aerospace engineer flew to the International Space Station twice, first as a 2016 European Space Agency flight engineer and again in 2021 aboard a SpaceX Crew Dragon — who is he?
Thomas Pesquet: French aerospace engineer, pilot, and astronaut.
Commonly nicknamed a "mini-stroke," this brief disruption of blood flow to the brain causes stroke-like symptoms that fully resolve within 24 hours — what medical event is it?
